releasesInRange.name: pnpm 12.16
releasesInRange.body:
This release adds a global `--env-file` flag, updates to a symlinked `pnpm-lock.yaml`, and `pnpm setup --no-modify-path`. It also fixes two security issues, in zstd decompression and in signing.

### Minor Changes

- Added a repeatable global `--env-file <path>` flag to load environment variables from dotenv-style files before running a command. Later files override earlier files, variables already in the environment are preserved, and loaded variables are visible to user-level `.npmrc` interpolation and lifecycle scripts [#7111](https://github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/7111).

- pnpm can now update a `pnpm-lock.yaml` that is a symlink. List the directories the lockfile may link into in the `symlinkedLockfileTargetDirs` setting, in the global config or with `PNPM_CONFIG_SYMLINKED_LOCKFILE_TARGET_DIRS`. pnpm writes the update to the file the symlink points to if that file is inside one of these directories. The symlink stays in place. pnpm ignores this setting in `pnpm-workspace.yaml` [#17222](https://github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/17222).

- Added a `--no-modify-path` option to `pnpm setup`. It installs pnpm without adding it to `PATH`, leaving the shell config file, the Windows registry, and the GitHub Actions environment files unchanged. `pnpm setup` then prints the lines to add yourself [get.pnpm.io#37](https://github.com/pnpm/get.pnpm.io/issues/37).

### Patch Changes

#### Security

- Fixed memory exposure and allocation handling vulnerabilities when processing zstd-compressed data [#17388](https://github.com/pnpm/pnpm/pull/17388).

- Signing in pnpm and pnpr no longer uses arithmetic that may leak the private key through timing. This covers shared artifacts, OCI registry tokens, and OIDC login state [advisory](https://rustsec.org/advisories/RUSTSEC-2026-0387).

#### Installing packages

- A dependency symlink that pnpm cannot point at the wanted target now fails the install with an error that names the link. This happens when the filesystem still serves the old link after pnpm removed it, as a `node_modules` served by a virtual filesystem does. pnpm used to remove the link again without end and crashed with a segmentation fault once the thread ran out of stack.

- Concurrent workspace installs no longer lose store-index rows when initializing the shared SQLite index [#17388](https://github.com/pnpm/pnpm/pull/17388).

- Agent skill links now keep the same target across installs when a package version is installed with several sets of peer dependencies. An install no longer fails with `ERR_PNPM_AGENT_SKILL_PATH_OCCUPIED` on a skill link that pnpm created for another of those copies [#17319](https://github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/17319).

- pnpm now fails at once, without retrying, when a downloaded package archive contains a rejected entry path [#17205](https://github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/17205).

- pnpm now builds a git-hosted dependency in every new location it links the dependency into, such as a new global virtual store slot or a fresh `node_modules
…(truncated)

releasesInRange.name: pnpm 11.28.9
releasesInRange.body:
This release fixes a crash on registry responses with too many content encodings ([GHSA-xjj6-f33q-929c](https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-xjj6-f33q-929c)) and sizes the install worker pool by the container's CPU quota. A repeat `pnpm install` now acts on more setting changes.

### Patch Changes

#### Crashes and security

* A registry response with too many content encodings can no longer crash pnpm. pnpm now uses undici 7.30.1, which fixes [GHSA-xjj6-f33q-929c](https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-xjj6-f33q-929c).

* `pnpm install` now sizes its worker pool by the CPU quota of the container it runs in, such as a Kubernetes CPU limit, when that quota is smaller than the number of CPUs the container may run on. The default `workspaceConcurrency` respects the quota the same way. On a CI runner with a 4-CPU quota and hundreds of host CPUs, pnpm started hundreds of workers and ran out of memory [#17382](https://github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/17382).

#### Repeat installs and changed settings

* A repeat `pnpm install` now acts on a change to these settings. Before, it reported "Already up to date".

  * `storeDir` or `virtualStoreDir`: it recreates `node_modules`.
  * `virtualStoreDirMaxLength`: it renames the virtual store directories.
  * `dangerouslyAllowAllBuilds` turned on: it runs the builds it skipped.
  * `trustLockfile` turned off: it verifies the lockfile.

* `pnpm add`, `pnpm remove`, and `pnpm update` now fail when the `node-linker` setting differs from the one recorded in `node_modules`. A `pnpm install` of the whole workspace recreates `node_modules` with the new `node-linker`, and an install filtered to some projects fails [pnpm/tasks#203](https://github.com/pnpm/tasks/issues/203).

* An install filtered to some workspace projects now fails if `node_modules` was installed with a different `nodeLinker`, `hoistPattern`, `publicHoistPattern`, store, or virtual store. Before, it recreated `node_modules` and left the projects it skipped without their dependencies. A `pnpm install` of the whole workspace still recreates `node_modules` [pnpm/tasks#217](https://github.com/pnpm/tasks/issues/217).

* `pnpm install` now takes its fast path in a workspace with `patchedDependencies` when the previous install ran with another major version of pnpm.

* `pnpm install` now relinks the bins of a workspace package when its `bin` field changes, including with `--frozen-lockfile` and an unchanged lockfile. A filtered install relinks them in the selected projects, and the next install that covers the remaining projects relinks them there [#17324](https://github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/17324).

* `pnpm install` now removes command shims from `node_modules/.bin` when a workspace dependency renames or removes an entry from its `bin` field [pnpm/tasks#211](https://github.com/pnpm/tasks/issues/211).

* With `nodeLinker: hoisted`, an install that stops partway no longer leaves the next install trusting the packages it was replacing. Before, reverting the change that sta

releasesInRange.name: pnpm 12.16.1
releasesInRange.body: This release fixes `pnpm install` hanging on a cold store in workspaces that install Cargo crates, and `pnpm pack` shipping a file that `files` excludes by name. ### Patch Changes - `pnpm install` no longer hangs on a cold store in a workspace that also installs Cargo crates or a Rust toolchain. - `pnpm pack` and `pnpm publish` now apply a `files` entry that names a file after the glob and directory entries, as npm does. A file excluded by name, such as `!dist/index.js`, stays out even when a later `dist/**` matches it. A file named by its path, such as `lib/secret.js`, ships even when a later `!lib/*.js` matches it. - `pnpm install` no longer leaves a broken symlink in an injected workspace dependency when the package links to a file outside its published files and pnpm imports by hardlink. Installing a git dependency now skips internal directory symlinks when importing its files into the store. - `pnpm install` now relinks a command that a workspace project renames into the projects that depend on it when `sharedWorkspaceLockfile` is `false` [pnpm/tasks#224](https://github.com/pnpm/tasks/issues/224). - `pnpm install` and `pnpm rebuild` now refresh privately hoisted `.bin` shims in `node_modules/.pnpm/node_modules/.bin` after a dependency build replaces a script target with a native executable [#17402](https://github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/17402). - `pnpm install` now reads a package's manifest to decide its peer dependencies when it updates an existing lockfile, as it does when it resolves from scratch. - Commands, `pnpm --version`, `pnpm self-update`, and invocations with unknown flags now apply the same `packageManager` and `devEngines.packageManager` settings when switching to the pinned pnpm version or recording it in `pnpm-lock.yaml`. `--config.` flags and `lockfileDir` now reach the version switch and lockfile sync on every entry point. Unreadable settings in `pnpm-workspace.yaml` or the global `config.yaml` that do not affect the pin decision no longer block the version switch [pnpm/tasks#222](https://github.com/pnpm/tasks/issues/222). - pnpm now accepts the `--cache-dir ` flag, as in `pnpm install --cache-dir /tmp/pnpm-cache` [#17422](https://github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/17422). - When the version or range given to `pnpm unpublish` matches every published version, the error now says so and shows the same command with `--force`. Before, the error suggested running `pnpm unpublish @`, the command that had just failed. ## Platinum Sponsors

prs.author: zkochan

fix(pnpr): preserve delegated registry aliases
prs.author: kairosci
prs.body:
## Summary

Closes pnpm/tasks#204.

A pnpr resolve request carries the client's registries as declarations keyed by URL, and each declaration held a single `prefix`. When a project routes two prefixes to one URL (for example `zeta` and `work` in `namedRegistries`), only the smallest one reached the server. A `zeta:^1.0.0` dependency then failed to resolve on the server, and an existing `foo@zeta:1.0.0` lockfile entry failed the server's undeclared-prefix check instead of being re-keyed to `work:`.

The request protocol now adds an `aliases` list next to `prefix`. `prefix` stays the smallest prefix, the one lockfile keys carry. `aliases` is part of the request protocol only: `pnpm-workspace.yaml` refuses it in both CLIs, so no new setting is added.

Both clients (v11 `toRegistryDeclarations`, v12 `to_declarations`) emit the aliases, and the server validates and routes them (`validate_declarations`, `declarations_into_lookups`).

The v11 config reader also stores prefix routes as own data properties, so a `registries` entry with `prefix: __proto__` is no longer silently dropped.

prs.title: fix(pacquet): reject ambiguous -T in pacquet add
prs.author: tats-u
prs.body:
## Summary

Related:

- https://github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/3868#issuecomment-956893168
- #12863

Both `--save-types` and `--tilde` options want `-T` as a shorthand, but it hasn't been settled which one it ultimately belongs to. Therefore, this PR will add `-T` as a hidden option for `pnpm add`, and if specified, list both long options to direct users to them.

> I think Yarn has this behavior by default. Doing it with the `-T` flag might be confusing as `-T,--tilde` means `--save-prefix=~` in Yarn.

## Squash Commit Body

```text
Reject `-T` on `add` with an error that names `--save-types` and `--tilde`.

`add` has both `--save-types` and `--tilde`. Accepting `-T` would force pnpm to
guess between two long options that are both valid for the command, so the
parser reports the ambiguity and points at the explicit spellings instead.

`-T` is declared as a hidden short flag on `add` and rejected in
`validate_command_scoped_global_options` after clap parses. Going through clap
keeps short clusters (`-DT`), attached values (`-CT`, `--save-prefix=-T`) and
tokens after `--` handled by clap's own rules. The `install <pkg>` -> `add`
rewrite runs before parsing, so `install foo -T` gets the same error. The flag
is hidden, so `-T` does not appear in the help text.

This change is v12-only. pnpm v11 does not expose both options on `add`.
```

prs.title: fix(store): keep packages that a project still uses on `store prune`
prs.author: leemr
prs.body:
## Summary

`pnpm store prune` removes packages that a project still uses when pnpm copied or cloned them into `node_modules`.  On Linux that's every patched or built package, and with `packageImportMethod: copy` or a macOS clone it's every package.  The next install then downloads them again.

I found this through a monorepo's CI, which ran `pnpm store prune` before saving the store cache so the cache wouldn't grow.  The first run on pnpm 12.15.0 printed `Removed 24 packages` from a fresh install, and the next run restored that cache, downloaded the same packages, and printed `Removed 24 packages` again.  Every one of the 24 was in `allowBuilds` or `patchedDependencies`.  So the cache never kept them.

The prune decides a CAS file is unused when it has one hard link.  A package that will be built or patched is imported with `clone-or-copy`, so the build or patch can't write through to the store, and its store files keep that one link while the project uses them.  The fix stops relying on the link count alone.  For each registered project, the prune reads the installed `node_modules/.pnpm/lock.yaml`, looks up each package's row in the store index, and keeps every file of the row, including every side-effects entry.  That covers patched, built, copied, and cloned packages, and runtimes like `node@runtime:`.  A project without that lockfile, or a package without a row, still falls back to the hard-link check.

prs.title: fix(pnpr): close each libsql connection once
prs.author: zkochan
prs.body:
## Summary

Windows Rust CI sometimes aborts a pnpr-auth libsql test with `0xc0000005: Invalid access to memory location`. There were four recent occurrences: three in `registration_cap_is_strict_across_backend_instances` and one, on main, in `sync_server::bulk_revocation_refreshes_a_replica_whose_tokens_went_elsewhere` ([run 40250430150](https://github.com/pnpm/pnpm/actions/runs/40250430150/job/121340967869)).

**Cause.** libsql closes every dropped local connection twice. `LibsqlConnection::drop` calls `disconnect()`, and then the inner `local::Connection`'s own `Drop` calls `disconnect()` again. Both calls see the `drop_ref` Arc as unique, so `sqlite3_close_v2` runs a second time on a handle SQLite has already freed. Usually that read of freed memory finds the "closed" state and SQLite reports misuse. If another thread has reused the memory, it reads garbage and crashes. The tests that crashed run several connections at once, which makes that reuse likely.

**Fix.** Upstream fixed this in tursodatabase/libsql#2261, released in 0.10.0: the handle is set to null after the first close. pnpr stays on the pnpm fork, because tursodatabase/libsql#2301 (HTTP connection reuse) is still unreleased. So the upstream commit is cherry-picked onto the fork's `pnpm-0.9.30` branch ([e2c44e6](https://github.com/pnpm/libsql/commit/e2c44e616a1f8e1ec7ceeb61138a3c2c391c35a9)), and this PR bumps the fork rev.

**Test.** `pnpr/crates/auth/tests/libsql_connection_close.rs` installs an SQLite log c
…(truncated)

prs.title: fix: fail on a locked optional dependency written with a named-registry specifier
prs.author: zkochan
prs.body:
## Summary

An optional dependency that fails to resolve is skipped unless the wanted lockfile already has an entry that satisfies it. That check only accepted plain semver ranges, so an optional dependency written with a named-registry prefix (`work:^1.0.0`) was always skipped on failure, even when the lockfile held `foo@work:1.2.0`. The skip then dropped the locked entries.

Both stacks now hand the specifier to the parser the lockfile-reuse gate already uses. It unwraps a declared prefix or built-in alias to its range and registry, and it matches only entries locked from that registry:

- v12: `wanted_lockfile_contains_satisfying_entry` replaces its plain-semver early return with the new `any_locked_key_admits`, which parses the specifier once through the parser behind `locked_child_admits`. It returns `false` without visiting the keys for a specifier the parser can't read, so git, tag, URL, and `jsr:` specifiers still skip.
- v11: `wantedLockfileContainsSatisfyingEntry` accepts a plain range or a `<prefix>:` specifier (new `isNamedRegistrySpecifier`) and checks each entry through `getRangeOfLockedPackage`. A plain range now also has to match the entry's registry, the same as v12 already did.

Closes https://github.com/pnpm/tasks/issues/210

prs.title: fix(deps-restorer): forget hoisted locations before replacing them
prs.author: zkochan
prs.body:
## Summary

Under `nodeLinker: hoisted`, both CLIs reuse a package at a location the previous install's `hoistedLocations` records, provided the on-disk `package.json` has the expected version. Nothing marked an install as in progress. If an install replaced a recorded location and stopped before `.modules.yaml` was written, the old record stayed behind. Reverting the change (a patch edit, or a resolution change that keeps the version) then made the next install reuse the half-replaced files.

Both CLIs now rewrite `.modules.yaml` before the hoisted linker touches the tree. The rewrite drops every recorded location this install does not reuse as is, which covers both locations it will re-import and orphans it will remove. A repeat install that reuses everything writes nothing extra.

Not covered: the short window between the final `.modules.yaml` write and the current lockfile write. In that window `.modules.yaml` already records the new content while the current lockfile still has the old resolution, so v12's `resolution_changed_at` check can still be fooled. prs.title: fix(install): re-resolve plain-keyed packages when their scope moves to another registry
prs.author: zkochan
prs.body:
## Summary

A plain lockfile key (`@scope/a@1.0.0`) records no registry, so the reuse gate read its registry from the current scope route. Routing a scope to another registry was invisible: the lockfile stayed fresh, the install went headless, and the locked versions and their children were fetched from the new registry with the old integrity. The install failed where resolving against the new registry would succeed. This affects pnpm v11 and v12 and predates pnpm/pnpm#17259.

Closes https://github.com/pnpm/tasks/issues/209.

Behavior:

- The workspace state records the scope routes the lockfile was resolved under (`registryRoutes`). A resolving unfiltered install records the routes it ran under; a frozen or filtered install keeps the previous record while a plain key still sits under a moved route.
- A plain key under a moved route marks the lockfile stale for a resolving install. The reuse gate reads a plain key's registry from the record, so the key is refused, loses its pin, and resolves again from its range against the new registry. `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile` installs the lockfile as recorded.
- A route change is a settings drift for the repeat-install shortcut and `verify-deps-before-run`.
- The default registry is not recorded: switching it is routinely a switch between mirrors and would resolve every unscoped package again. Only scope routes are tracked, which is what the task asks for.
- The `route:` entries of `registryPrefixes` were redundant with the new rec

prs.title: fix(lockfile.verification): reuse local dependency walks per importer
prs.author: kairosci
prs.body:
## Summary

Closes pnpm/pnpm#17374.

The v11 lockfile check walked each direct `file:` dependency's local directory subtree with a fresh visited map. A project whose direct local dependencies share transitive local directories (the issue's 5×40 DAG) re-walked the shared graph once per direct dependency. The check now creates one checker per importer, so all of an importer's direct local dependencies share the visited snapshots and peer scopes.

pnpm v12 is not affected (see the issue), so this is a v11-only fix.

The checker collects the lockfile's recorded peers on its first check, so a project with no local directory dependency pays nothing extra.

### Measurements

The issue's `compact-repro.mjs` (200 `file:` packages, 5 levels × 40), Node 24, Linux. Same bundle, three runs each. The baseline patches the shared map back to a fresh one per direct dependency.

| phase | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| seed | 1538–1691 ms | 1430–1493 ms |
| repeat | 1729–1786 ms | 362–378 ms |
| frozen | 1002–1027 ms | 342–349 ms |

The lockfile stayed unchanged in every run.

## Squash Commit Body

```text
checkLinkedPackagesAreUpToDate creates one local directory checker per
importer. Its checks share the `visited` map and the recorded peers, so a
snapshot reached through several direct dependencies is walked once per
peer scope instead of once per direct dependency.

prs.title: refactor(pacquet): name how much of the lockfile an install resolved
fix(executor): keep the group watchdog's pipe out of concurrent spawns
prs.author: zkochan
prs.body:
## Summary

Fixes the macOS flake of `interrupt::killing_the_process_group_of_pnpm_kills_every_script_of_a_parallel_run`, and the real bug behind it.

macOS has no `pipe2`, so Rust's std creates a pipe with `pipe()` and sets `FD_CLOEXEC` on each end afterwards (`library/std/src/sys/pipe/unix.rs`). A parallel run spawns its scripts from several threads. If one script is forked between the `pipe()` and the `fcntl` of the watchdog's stdin, that script inherits the write end of the watchdog's lifeline. Once pnpm is killed, that script still holds the pipe open. The watchdog never reads end of input, so it kills no group. The test then waits out its one-minute deadline on the first script and kills it. If that script held the pipe, the watchdog finally sees end of input and ends the rest, which is why a single survivor is reported.

The fix adds a process-wide `RwLock`. Every spawn of the executor crate (`spawn_child`, the `ps` listing used on cancellation, and the plain shell spawn) holds it shared around `Command::spawn`, so scripts still spawn concurrently. The watchdog's spawn holds it exclusively, so no fork happens while the watchdog's pipe is inheritable. The watchdog also can no longer inherit a script's output pipe, which would have kept pnpm from seeing that script's end of output. Linux uses `pipe2(O_CLOEXEC)` and was never affected, which matches the test passing there.

pnpm v11 has no group watchdog, so this is v12 only.

Closes pnpm/tasks#216

Spawns in other crates

prs.author: zkochan
prs.body:
## Summary

Closes pnpm/pnpm#17382

Related to pnpm/pnpm#17384, which fixes the same issue through the `node-cpu-count` package plus a fixed cap of 16 default workers. This PR reads the cgroup files itself with no new dependency, walks the full cgroup hierarchy for v2, keeps the default worker count uncapped on hosts without a quota, and applies the quota to the `workspaceConcurrency` default too. pnpm 11 sized its worker pool and the default `workspaceConcurrency` from `os.availableParallelism()`, which counts the CPUs in the process's affinity mask. In a container whose cgroup CPU quota is far smaller than that mask (the report: a 4-CPU Kubernetes limit on a 233-CPU node), each install created 232 workers, and four concurrent installs ran a 16 GiB memory limit dry while the workers were still loading.

prs.author: lazerg
prs.body:
## Summary

Closes pnpm/pnpm#17387.

Once the live frame grows taller than the terminal, every new line went through the overflow handover from pnpm/pnpm#14270: the differ shrank the frame to the line being committed, erased everything below it, and a fresh differ drew the whole visible frame again. `pnpm run --stream` adds one line per line of script output, so each line rewrote the full screen. prs.author: kairosci

## Summary

Closes pnpm/pnpm#17395.

With `nodeLinker: hoisted` and `autoInstallPeers: false`, pnpm v12 wrote only one copy of a package that two workspace projects use with different peer versions. The second project then resolved the first project's peer. pnpm v11 nests the second variant, so this is a v12-only regression and v11 needs no change.

The fix has two halves, and the new end-to-end test fails without either one:

- The hoister keeps a peer-bearing node's own snapshot key as its reference instead of collapsing it onto the first-seen variant. Distinct locators make the hoister nest the variant where its peers differ.
- The hoisted dep-graph walk indexes locations by exact snapshot key as well as by package id. A project's direct dependency and a package's child edge resolve to the copy of their own variant before falling back to the package id.

### Why not keep the collapse and fix only the hoister

The collapse was added because distinct variant references once made the hoister run out of memory on a large lockfile. An alternative that keeps the collapse and adds upstream yarn's peer check to the dedup path does place the copies correctly. The walker then cannot tell the two variants apart, because both copies carry the same snapshot key. v12's hoisted linker treats copies with the same key as duplicates: it builds one and symlinks the others. That cross-links the variants again.
